title: Contraste y concesión: aunque, mientras que, sin embargo

sections.content: Aunque admits a fact and immediately qualifies it within the same sentence; mientras que sets two facts side by side as a direct contrast; sin embargo opens a new sentence that pushes back against what came before. All three let a text hold an official claim and a messier reality in view at once. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: El Estado presentaba el territorio como una unidad natural, aunque en la práctica existían pueblos cuya vida ignoraba esas líneas.
items.english: The state presented the territory as a natural unity, although in practice there were peoples whose lives ignored those lines.

items.spanish: Mientras que las fronteras modernas fueron trazadas por acuerdos diplomáticos, las comunidades aymaras habían mantenido redes que cruzaban esas zonas.
items.english: While modern borders were drawn by diplomatic agreements, Aymara communities had maintained networks that crossed those areas.

items.spanish: El Estado, sin embargo, insistía en presentar a sus ciudadanos como una comunidad nacional homogénea.
items.english: The state, however, insisted on presenting its citizens as a homogeneous national community.

items.spanish: Los aymaras continuaron practicando vínculos transfronterizos, aunque las autoridades los reconocieran cada vez menos.
items.english: The Aymara kept practicing cross-border ties, even though the authorities recognized them less and less.

sections.content: Aunque + subjunctive (aunque las autoridades... reconocieran) signals that the concession is about an ongoing attitude, not a settled fact — compare it with aunque + indicative, which would present the concession as simply true. Both are common; the subjunctive version here softens it slightly toward 'even granting that...'
